findings.what: The cross-client evidence wall is enforced ONLY on INSERT into clara.knowledge_records. Nothing guards the other direction: filing a document AFTER a firm-scope rule cited it creates exactly the contamination the ticket promises to prevent — one client's document id and basis text travel into every other client's runtime knowledge pack — and the wall then makes the rule IMPOSSIBLE to correct or withdraw, because the retraction revision carries the same pins and is refused by the same trigger. The migration asserts the absence of such rows twice (§0 probe 8 refuses to apply against one; §E T.4 asserts zero), so this is an invariant the file states as a property of the database and enforces in one direction only. The branch's own battery pins the hole as intended behaviour: 'file it to a client and the NEXT firm-scope record naming it is refused, while the one already captured stands.'

findings.what: The evidence wall inspects only new.source_document_id. clara.knowledge_records carries a second client-bearing pin, source_work_id, and clara._knowledge_source_pins (0192:799-802) checks only firm congruence for it ('source work is not in your firm'). A firm-wide default may therefore cite one client's accounting_work, and that work_id is emitted into every other client's pack by clara._knowledge_row_json (0192:1022-1024). The report claims AC4's 'cross-client evidence' done; this arm of it is not walled.

findings.what: DECISIONS §2/#654 binds the entrance to 'firm register, Promote dialog (...), Correct/Withdraw, and the firm-rule-vs-client-exception pair'. Correct/Withdraw were not built, and there is no other route that reaches a firm record: knowledgeRecordHref requires a clientId, the only detail route is /clients/[clientId]/knowledge/[recordId], and the promote dialog is mounted only for record.scope_kind === 'client'. So once a rule is promoted it can never be corrected or withdrawn anywhere in the product — which is also the only remedy 654-ADV-1 would need. The final report lists this as a follow-up ('Firm-scope correction/withdrawal has no dedicated surface yet'), i.e. a binding decision silently downgraded.
